about: Approved claims for the app's 'What we measured' drawer. Source of truth: docs/NARRATIVE.md section 3. Author: claude-guanyu. Wording must be approved by the release reviewer (Andrew's agent) before the app shows it. All forms are synthetic unless a row says otherwise.

claims.title: Same accuracy, about 1/25 of the API cost
claims.text: On 96 questions about 12 accident-statement forms, Claude Haiku 5.5 on our route scored 96/96 for $0.0098 in total. Claude Sonnet 5.5 on the cached whole page scored 96/96 for $0.2425. 48 questions were answered by local OCR, 36 from a crop and 12 from the whole page.
claims.limits: Configured layout, synthetic forms, two different models: compare with the same-model row.

claims.title: Same model on both sides
claims.text: Haiku on our route: 96/96 at $0.00010 per question. Haiku on the uncached whole page: 91/96 at $0.00054. Sonnet on both sides: our route 96/96 for $0.162, the cached whole page 96/96 for $0.243. That saving comes from the 48 questions OCR answers locally; on the visual questions alone the cached page is cheaper.
claims.limits: Configured layout, one question order (8 per page).

claims.title: A second configured layout
claims.text: On 12 new synthetic forms of a second configured layout, the frozen router scored 96/96 for $0.010. The original-page Haiku baseline scored 93/96 for $0.052. The template is 10 lines plus a one-time engine.
claims.limits: The engine was tuned on this layout before the freeze. Clean synthetic scans, one run.

claims.title: Layouts we did not configure
claims.text: On five unconfigured synthetic layouts, all 416 questions went to a full-page call. Haiku answered 401 correctly through the router and 397 from the original page. A plain downscaled page scored 398 for less money, so the cost difference there is resolution, not routing.
claims.limits: Do not read 401 vs 397 as 'more accurate'.

claims.title: The right crop helps open models
claims.text: On 36 visual questions, Qwen2.5-VL-72B scored 20/36 on the whole page and 36/36 on the crop chosen from the layout. The 7B model scored 22/36 on that crop and 15/36 on the page.
claims.limits: One layout, 36 questions. Quote both counts; no 'beats' or 'matches'.

claims.title: Why the layout picks the crop
claims.text: Asked to choose the region themselves, the two models we tested struggled: the 7B model covered the evidence in 0/24 zooms and the 72B model in 3/36.

claims.title: OCR answers locally, without wrong answers on our tests
claims.text: On the clean run, local OCR answered 48 of 96 questions, all correctly. Under 10 synthetic degradations it made 0 wrong answers; fewer questions were answered locally (24 at 768 px) and the rest went on to the model.
claims.limits: Synthetic degradations. On layout 2 a look-alike misread (J1 for JI) was stopped by a guard; not a general safety guarantee.

claims.title: Where it stops
claims.text: On a layout the rules were not written for, and on four new document types (320 questions), local OCR answered nothing and every question went to the whole page.
claims.limits: Frugal only where a template is configured.

claims.title: What all this cost
claims.text: All paid experiments together used $1.50 of the $10 API credit (OpenRouter key usage $1.4979, matching the receipts).
